<thought>The 13C NMR shows peaks at 54.00 ppm and 43.70 ppm, which are typical for methyl carbons attached to heteroatoms (e.g., O‑CH₃, N‑CH₃). No upfield methyl signals (~10‑30 ppm) are present. To confirm the presence of two methyl groups, a ¹H NMR spectrum can be examined for two singlets integrating to three protons each. However, based on the carbon data alone, the most plausible interpretation is that the molecule contains two CH₃ groups.</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
